findings.title: Mixed save taps can hand over duplicates
findings.description: `save(p)` does not check whether Save all is busy or whether its PID is already handed over, while Save all continues through a snapshot of files taken before its download waits. Tapping a photo during a batch can download it immediately and again when the batch reaches it; a pending individual share can likewise overlap a Save all share.

evidence.explanation: Only `tap()` checks `busy`; `save(p)` starts its own handoff without reading that state. The batch captures `ready` once and waits between downloads without rechecking `handed`, so an individual tap can hand over a later snapshot entry first.

findings.title: Blocked downloads disappear from retries
findings.description: `tap()` marks a photo as handed over whenever `downloadFile()` returns, but that function only clicks an anchor and cannot establish that the browser accepted the download. If the browser blocks later files in a batch, the next tap excludes them and says there is nothing new to save.

citations.citation: Chrome lists Automatic downloads among site permissions and explains that a site permission can be blocked.

evidence.explanation: The download callback returns after `a.click()` without a completion signal, while the batch immediately adds that photo's PID to `handed`. Chrome documents Automatic downloads as a site permission that can be blocked; the next batch filters out every handed PID.

findings.title: Save all misses photos during verification
findings.description: `saveBatch()` sees a photo neither as ready nor as arriving between removal from `incoming` and insertion into `files`. The receive path awaits checksum verification during that interval, so a tap then reports “Nothing new to save” even though the full photo is finishing.

evidence.explanation: The final chunk removes its `incoming` entry before calling `done()`. `done()` awaits SHA-256 before adding the File, whereas `saveBatch` reads only `files` for ready photos and `incoming` for arriving ones.

findings.title: A stuck share blocks later Save all taps
findings.description: `tap()` keeps `busy` true until the promise from `share(list)` settles, with no recovery path if it never does. After a browser share operation remains pending, every later Save all tap returns “Still saving,” including taps for photos received afterward.

evidence.explanation: The only reset of `busy` is in `finally`, which is reached only when the awaited share returns or rejects. The guard then prevents every later Save all attempt.

findings.title: Failed downloads go unreported to people
findings.description: The batch download loop catches exceptions from `download()` but only sends them to `console.warn`. When an object URL cannot be created or an anchor click throws, the earlier “Downloading” toast remains the only user-facing result even though that photo was left for a retry.

evidence.explanation: `downloadFile` uses browser operations that can throw, and its wrapper is passed into `createSaveAll`. The catch logs failures without calling `toast`; the test's throwing download confirms this path leaves a PID unhanded for a later retry.

findings.title: One failed share stops future share sheets
findings.description: `downloadNext` becomes true after any non-cancellation share rejection and is never cleared after the fallback batch. Once a phone has used the prompted download fallback, later newly received photos also bypass its available share sheet for the rest of the tab session.

evidence.explanation: The flag is initialized false, set true on rejection and read before every subsequent batch, but never reset. The test exercises only the immediately following fallback tap, not a later batch.
